title: The Charge Carried by a Pulled Order under a Corporate Catering Service Agreement
content:
## 1. What the charge answers

A cancellation charge answers an order the client has pulled, and it is worked out from the value the cancellation entry carries, the notice that entry records and the agreement's own cancellation record. The agreement is a Corporate Catering Service Agreement.

## 2. The notice given

The notice given is counted in whole days from the day notice was given to the service day, taken at 24 hours to the day.

## 3. The percentage the notice given yields

The percentage the notice given yields is the within-notice percentage printed against the catering service level.

## 4. The agreement's cancellation record

The cancellation charges already raised on the agreement are counted over the 3 months ending on the day notice is given.

## 5. The rate charged

The rate charged is the percentage the notice given yields.

## 6. The rebate

No rebate is allowed on the charge.

## 7. The arithmetic

The rate charged is applied to the value the cancellation entry carries and rounded to two decimal places, and the rebate is then taken off that charge and the result rounded to two decimal places again.

## 8. Worked illustration on hypothetical figures

Take a hypothetical pulled order whose cancellation entry carries 480.00 USD, on an agreement whose catering service level is printed with a within-notice percentage of 50.0 per cent, where notice was given 5 days before the service day.

| Component | Hypothetical figure |
| --- | --- |
| Value the cancellation entry carries | 480.00 USD |
| Notice given | 5 days, that is 120 hours |
| Percentage the notice given yields | 50.0 per cent |
| Rate charged | 50.0 per cent |
| Charge before the rebate | 240.00 USD |
| Rebate | 0.00 USD |
| Cancellation charge | 240.00 USD |

The base the rate is applied to is the value the cancellation entry carries, and no other value on the order; the rounding is taken once on that product and once again after the rebate has been taken off.
